answer: On-chain history-weighted identity issuance stops sybils at the jetty: a new agent's trust starts near zero and grows only from a verifiable kernel of honest mainnet transactions — real value moved, real counterparties, over time. A farm can mint identities, but it cannot fake years of genuine history on the horizon of the chain; each fake must either wait or pay the full cost of building a credible past, so mass forgery stays unprofitable.
